proposed_quote: The alternative secretion pathway which exports hemolysin across both Escherichia coli membranes into the surrounding medium is directed by an uncleaved C-terminal targeting signal and the membrane translocator proteins HlyD and HlyB.
notes: Cited ref PMID 3891743 (Felmlee 1985, 10.1128/jb.163.1.94-105.1985) is a nucleotide-sequencing paper; quote is verbatim from its abstract but is about predicted molecular masses of the hlyCABD cistrons, NOT secretion; abstract documents no secretion assay. Organism (E. coli HlyA) correct. Proposed Koronakis/Hughes/Koronakis 1991 EMBO J (PMID 1915293) which directly documents HlyB/HlyD-dependent secretion of HlyA across both E. coli membranes (T1SS). Checked PMIDs 3891743,1915293,2274026,1791766.

PMID 2185213 (Highlander 1990, 10.1128/jb.172.5.2343-2350.1990) title 'Secretion and expression of the Pasteurella haemolytica Leukotoxin'. Quote verbatim in abstract. LktA (M./P. haemolytica) secreted via HlyB/HlyD heteroplasmid complementation = T1SS export. Organism matches (Mannheimia/Pasteurella haemolytica).

PMID 17116373 (Crosby & Kachlany 2006, 10.1016/j.gene.2006.10.004), TdeA TolC-like protein. All three '...'-joined quote fragments verbatim in abstract: 'produces leukotoxin (LtxA), a member of the RTX family of toxins'; 'an outer membrane channel-forming protein, TolC, is required for toxin secretion'; 'requires a TolC-like protein for LtxA secretion'. tdeA mutant did not secrete LtxA = machinery-dependent secretion (T1SS OMP). Organism A. actinomycetemcomitans matches.

Cited ref PMID 9244262 (Akatsuka 1997, 10.1128/jb.179.15.4754-4760.1997). Quote verbatim in abstract, BUT the 'PrtA' in that sentence is Serratia marcescens PrtA (stated 'shows homology to the Erwinia chrysanthemi metalloproteases'), secreted heterologously via the E. chrysanthemi PrtDEF exporter. Row protein Q07295 is the Dickeya/Erwinia chrysanthemi PrtA (serralysin A, UniProt confirms). This ref demonstrates the cognate Erwinia T1SS exporter works but does not directly show the Erwinia PrtA itself secreted; secretion link for the exact protein rests on homology/heterologous-exporter argument. Flag for human review; a dedicated Erwinia PrtA secretion ref (Delepelaire/Wandersman/Ghigo lineage) would be stronger. Checked PMID 9244262.

proposed_quote: One of the secreted proteins is PrtA, which is shown here to be a repeats-in-toxin (RTX) alkaline zinc metalloprotease.
notes: PMID 12777498 (Bowen 2003, 10.1099/mic.0.26171-0). Cited quote 'The prtA gene resides in a locus encoding both the protease ABC transporter (prtBCD) and an intervening ORF encoding a protease inhibitor (inh).' IS verbatim in abstract but describes locus/gene organization, not secretion. Ref does document secretion (abstract: 'One of the secreted proteins is PrtA...'; prtBCD = T1SS ABC exporter). Proposed verbatim secretion sentence from same ref. Organism Photorhabdus luminescens matches.

Cited DOI 10.1016/S0021-9258(18)81905-6 = PMID 2722818 (Delepelaire & Wandersman 1989, JBC 264:9083, 'Protease secretion by Erwinia chrysanthemi. Proteases B and C are synthesized and secreted as zymogens without a signal peptide.'). All three '...'-joined quote fragments verbatim in abstract: 'The gene encoding the secreted 53-kDa metalloprotease (protease B)'; 'do not have typical signal sequences at their NH2 termini'; 'secreted into the external medium'. Signal-peptide-independent export to external medium = T1SS. Organism E. chrysanthemi matches. Crossref/EuropePMC returned no abstract for the DOI but PubMed pii confirms identity.

PMID 9244262 (Akatsuka 1997, 10.1128/jb.179.15.4754-4760.1997). Quote 'LipA, HasA, and E. chrysanthemi PrtC were secreted via heterologous exporters and via some hybrid exporters.' verbatim in abstract. E. chrysanthemi PrtC secreted via ABC (T1SS) exporters. Organism matches.

PMID 17098895 (Kehl-Fie & St Geme 2006, 10.1128/JB.01319-06). Quote 'Using mariner mutagenesis and a screen for loss of cytotoxicity, a genetic locus encoding an RTX toxin system was identified.' verbatim in abstract. Organism Kingella kingae matches (UniProt A1YKW7 = Cytolysin RtxA). BUT abstract/accessible text documents cytotoxicity and RTX-locus identification, not a secretion assay (no supernatant detection or secretion-machinery-dependent export shown); T1SS secretion of RtxA rests on RTX-family classification. Full text not PMC-accessible. Flag for human review.
